title: Reel: marketplace seller? Two things your ads still tell you
hook: Most of your orders come from marketplaces. Your ads still have two things to tell you.
caption:
Most of your orders come from marketplaces. Your ads still have two things to tell you.

The sale may land elsewhere, but the attention data is yours.

1. Which first shot makes people stop. Check hook rate by ad, then try the winner as your first listing image.
2. Which reason to buy holds people longest. Check hold rate, then put that reason in your listing title and first bullet.

Both are tests worth running this week. Follow @galvor.ai.
alt_text: Reel cover in Galvor violet and gold reading: Marketplace seller? Read your ads anyway. The reel shows an ad's first shot moving into a marketplace listing image, and its reason to buy moving into the listing title. End card: follow @galvor.ai.

script.setup: Idea: a D2C founder whose orders mostly come through marketplaces, and who has written off Meta ad data because the sale lands elsewhere, gets two things to pull from the ads and use on the listing. On-screen title: Marketplace seller? Read your ads anyway. Expectation set: a reason ads still matter. The script beats it with two places on the listing to use what the ads show. Outline: attention data is yours (the turn); first shot to listing image (second-best, first); reason to buy to title and first bullet (best).

scenes.visual: An order arrow leaves an ad and lands on a generic marketplace box. The ad's dashboard looks empty.
scenes.voiceover: Most of your orders come from marketplaces. So ads teach nothing?
scenes.on_screen: Marketplace seller? Read your ads anyway.

scenes.visual: Two meters appear on the ad itself, labelled stopped and stayed.
scenes.voiceover: The sale may land elsewhere. The attention data is still yours.

scenes.visual: The two meters move to the centre, numbered one and two.
scenes.voiceover: Here are two things your ads can still tell you.

scenes.visual: Three dummy ads sit side by side. The opening frame of one glows.
scenes.voiceover: One: which first shot makes people stop. Check hook rate by ad.

scenes.visual: The glowing frame slides into the first image slot of a generic product listing.
scenes.voiceover: Try the winner as your first listing image.

scenes.visual: The listing's title line is blank and blinking.
scenes.voiceover: The bigger one is why they'd buy at all.

scenes.visual: Lines of ad copy appear with a watch-time bar under each. One bar is longest.
scenes.voiceover: Two: which reason to buy holds people longest. Check hold rate.

scenes.visual: The winning line moves into the listing title and the first bullet.
scenes.voiceover: Put that reason in your listing title and first bullet.

scenes.visual: End card with the Galvor logo. Chime.
scenes.voiceover: Ads are research, wherever the order lands. Follow @galvor.ai.

script.music: Light instrumental bed, low under the voice. Soft chime on the end card only.
script.notes: AI voiceover over motion graphics. No presenter and no first person singular. Captions burned in for muted viewing. Use dummy ad tiles only, never a client account or name. No numbers used. Use a generic listing layout. Do not name or imitate any marketplace, and do not show a real product.

slides.headline: Marketplace seller? *Read your ads anyway.*
slides.sub: Two things they still tell you.

slides.headline: Your ads are *research,* wherever the order lands.
slides.sub: First shot to image. Reason to buy to title.

notes:
Kept the topic and made it specific: two readings from the ads and where each goes on a listing. Both are framed as tests to run, with no promised result. No numbers used. No marketplace named. Slide 1 is the cover, slide 2 the end card.
